claims.claim: The first nylon (nylon 66) was synthesized on February 28, 1935, by Wallace Hume Carothers at DuPont's Experimental Station.
claims.episode_span: At DuPont in 1935, Wallace Carothers and his team polymerized nylon to create a fiber stronger than silk and cheaper to manufacture at scale.
claims.supporting_quote: The first nylon,  nylon 66 , was synthesized on February 28, 1935, by Wallace Hume Carothers at DuPont's research facility at the  DuPont Experimental Station .

claims.claim: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) was patented in 1941 by John Rex Whinfield and James Tennant Dickson of the Calico Printers' Association in Manchester, England.
claims.episode_span: British chemists John Whinfield and James Dickson followed in 1941 with polyethylene terephthalate, later branded Terylene and Dacron.
claims.supporting_quote: PET was patented in 1941 by  John Rex Whinfield , James Tennant Dickson and their employer the  Calico Printers' Association  of  Manchester , England.

claims.claim: Nylon stockings reached national U.S. stores in May 1940.
claims.episode_span: Nylon stockings reached American stores in 1940
claims.supporting_quote: Actual nylon stockings were not shipped to selected stores in the national market until May 15, 1940.

claims.claim: Washing synthetic garments sheds large numbers of microplastic fibers — more than 1,900 fibers per garment per wash, with fleeces shedding the most.
claims.episode_span: each agitation cycle sheared off thousands of microscopic polymer strands that passed straight through municipal filters
claims.supporting_quote: Each garment in a load of laundry can shed more than 1900 fibers of microplastics, with fleeces releasing the highest percentage of fibers

claims.claim: Microplastics have been found in human placentas, breast milk, and other body tissues and fluids.
claims.episode_span: These particles now appear in Arctic sea ice, alpine snow, table salt, and, most recently, meconium and placental tissue.
claims.supporting_quote: Even babies contain microplastics, from the placenta and breast milk. The brain, heart, and fluids such as urine have been found to have traces of microplastics

claims.claim: A single synthetic garment can shed >1,900 microplastic fibers per wash (Browne 2011)
claims.episode_span: A 2011 study in Environmental Science & Technology found that a single synthetic garment could shed more than 1,900 fibers in one wash; later work measured over 700,000 fibers released from an average 6-kilogram load.
claims.supporting_quote: Each garment in a load of laundry can shed more than 1900 fibers of microplastics

claims.claim: Later work measured over 700,000 fibers released from a ~6 kg wash load
claims.episode_span: A 2011 study in Environmental Science & Technology found that a single synthetic garment could shed more than 1,900 fibers in one wash; later work measured over 700,000 fibers released from an average 6-kilogram load.
claims.supporting_quote: over 700,000 fibers could be released per wash.
